passage: At the school gate in Bhopal, Pankaj's classmate Uma said, “Come on, everyone does it. Just skip the quiz. You have to decide right now!” Pankaj felt his stomach tighten. He asked, “What's the reason?” Uma shrugged. “Because it's fun.” Pankaj said, “Let me think about it.” He walked away and found Ms. Nair, the counsellor. He told her that Uma was pressing him to hide from the quiz, and that she also had asked him to keep it secret. Ms. Nair thanked him. “Taking time and telling me was the right thing.” Pankaj felt his shoulders drop.

qa.q: Who did Pankaj tell about the pressure?
qa.a: Ms. Nair, the counsellor.

qa.q: What was Pankaj feeling when Uma said everyone does it, and how do you know?
qa.a: He felt pressured and uneasy, since his stomach tightened, and he asked for a reason and time to think.

qa.q: Which habit helped Pankaj most?
qa.a: Asking what the reason was, taking time to think and telling a trusted adult about the pressure and the secret.

qa.q: How might Uma see Pankaj's walking away?
qa.a: She may feel annoyed that he did not go along, or she may not have thought it through, since her only reason was that it was fun.

grounding: A child notices everyone does it and pressure to decide quickly, asks what the reason is, takes time and tells a trusted adult.

passage: From the back of the classroom I saw Sabina talk to Karthik at the desk. “Everyone in Class 7 is doing it,” she said. “You have to decide by the bell, or you'll miss out.” Karthik looked at his shoes, then said, “Why?” Sabina said, “Because everyone is.” He didn't answer for a bit. “I want to think,” he said. Sabina said, “You'll regret it!” Karthik took his bag and walked to the teacher's desk. I couldn't hear what he said, but he looked calmer afterwards. I don't know what she wanted, but his questions seemed sensible.

qa.q: Who did Karthik go to after Sabina's talk?
qa.a: The teacher, at the teacher's desk.

qa.q: What was Karthik probably feeling when Sabina told him to decide by the bell?
qa.a: He probably felt pressured and unsure, so he asked why and said he wanted to think.

qa.q: What habit did Karthik show that others can copy?
qa.a: He asked for the reason, took time to think and went to a trusted adult.

qa.q: How might Sabina see Karthik's decision to walk away?
qa.a: She may feel frustrated or worried he would miss out, though the observer cannot know what she wanted.

grounding: A child notices the everyone does it appeal and pressure to decide quickly, asks the reason, takes time and goes to a trusted adult, seen by an observer.

passage: Monday: Aditi waved a pack of glitter stickers. “Everyone's buying these. Decide now; there are only two left!” Irfan almost handed over his canteen money. Then he asked, “What's the reason I need them?” Aditi shrugged. He kept his money. Wednesday: After school, some older kids said, “Everyone climbs the old water tank. You have to do it today, or you're a baby. And don't tell anyone.” Irfan's heart raced. Everyone, today, don't tell: the same pushing as the stickers, only scarier. He said, “No,” walked back inside and told Rao Sir at the gate. Rao Sir went straight to the tank, sent the kids home and had the ladder chained that evening. Friday: The ladder stayed chained.

qa.q: What did Rao Sir have done to the ladder?
qa.a: He had the ladder chained that evening.

qa.q: What was Irfan feeling when the older kids pushed the dare?
qa.a: Irfan felt scared, his heart racing, and recognised the same pushing as with the stickers.

qa.q: What did Irfan do on Wednesday, and why was it right?
qa.a: He said no, went inside and told Rao Sir the same day, because a pushed dare and a secret should always be told to a trusted adult.

qa.q: How did Aditi respond when Irfan asked the reason?
qa.a: Aditi just shrugged, showing she had no real reason beyond “everyone” and hurry.

grounding: Shows a child spotting everyone-does-it and hurry-up pressure, asking for the reason, and telling a trusted adult about a pushed dare.

passage: Shankar, that boy told you to swap your cricket cards now, before you could think? Let your Uma Paati tell you about the magic pen. At the temple fair when I was nine, a man shouted, “Magic pen! Never runs out! Every city child has one! Only ten left, today only!” People pushed forward. I had my festival coins in my fist. I wanted it so badly my hand was sweating. But my father always asked, “What's the reason?” So I asked the man, “How does it never run out?” He said, “Magic,” and turned to the next child. That wasn't a reason. I kept my coins. Two days later, my friend's magic pen was dry.

qa.q: What did the man claim the pen could do?
qa.a: He claimed it never runs out.

qa.q: What was young Uma feeling as she held her coins?
qa.a: She felt eager and tempted, wanting the pen so badly her hand was sweating.

qa.q: What choice did Uma make, and why was it wise?
qa.a: She asked for the reason, and when the man only said “Magic”, she kept her coins instead of rushing.

qa.q: How did Uma's friend come out of it?
qa.a: Uma's friend bought a magic pen that was dry two days later.

grounding: Shows a child noticing everyone-has-one and today-only pressure, asking what the reason is and taking time.

passage: It was late, and Farida was supposed to be asleep. A message popped up in the game chat from Kamal_07, a player she'd been teaming up with for a week. “Everyone in our clan sends a photo to join the secret team. Send yours now, tonight only. Don't tell your parents, they won't get it.” Farida's thumb hovered. Everyone. Now. Don't tell. Her stomach went cold. Those were exactly the words her teacher had told them to watch for. She didn't reply. She blocked Kamal_07, got out of bed and went to her mother's room with the tablet. Her mother read it, hugged her, said she'd done exactly the right thing, and reported the account with her before they both went back to bed.

qa.q: What did Kamal_07 ask Farida to send?
qa.a: Kamal_07 asked for a photo to join the secret team.

qa.q: What was Farida feeling when her stomach went cold?
qa.a: Farida felt frightened and uneasy, recognising the pressure words her teacher had warned about.

qa.q: Which of Farida's steps were right?
qa.a: She didn't reply, blocked the contact and told her mother that same night, and her mother reported the account with her.

qa.q: How did Farida's mother respond?
qa.a: Her mother hugged her, said she'd done exactly the right thing and reported the account with her before bed.

grounding: Shows a child spotting everyone-does-it, hurry and secrecy pressure from an online contact, ending contact and telling a trusted adult the same night.

passage:
The lift in Sai Towers was stuck again, so Chandrika and Keerthana climbed the stairs with their school bags. On the fourth floor, Keerthana stopped. "Tonight at nine, we're all climbing the gate to the closed pool. Everyone from C-block is coming. Say yes now, or you're out. And don't tell anyone."
Chandrika noticed how fast she was talking, and that "everyone" had no names. "Why at night? What's the reason?"
"Because it's fun. Stop asking."
Chandrika said she would think about it. Upstairs, she sat beside Amma, who was cutting beans, and told her everything. Amma put the knife down. "You did right to ask, and right to tell me." Within the hour Amma had spoken to the society guard about the pool gate and called Keerthana's mother.

qa.q: At what time was the group planning to climb the pool gate?
qa.a: At nine that night.

qa.q: What did Chandrika's question about the reason suggest she was feeling?
qa.a: She felt uneasy and suspicious of the rush, the secrecy and an 'everyone' with no names, though she may also have been worried about being left out.

qa.q: What did Amma do that kept the children safe?
qa.a: She listened, told Chandrika she was right to ask and to tell, and within the hour spoke to the guard about the gate and called Keerthana's mother.

qa.q: How might Keerthana see Chandrika's refusal to answer straight away?
qa.a: Keerthana might feel annoyed or let down, since she wanted a quick yes, and later perhaps embarrassed or relieved that an adult stepped in.

grounding: It shows a child spotting 'everyone is doing it' and rush-to-decide pressure, asking for the reason, and telling a trusted adult about a pushed secret dare.
